content: 1. Nevirapine reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of ziprasidone by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear but considered minor. 2. Nevirapine decreases zolpidem levels or effects through CYP3A4 induction. The clinical relevance is unknown but likely minor. 3. Nevirapine reduces zonisamide levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is uncertain but minor. 4. Both abacavir and nevirapine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Close monitoring is advised when these drugs are co-administered. 5. Nevirapine significantly reduces abemaciclib levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative therapies should be considered. Strong CYP3A4 inducers reduce abemaciclib plasma concentrations and its metabolites, necessitating close monitoring. 6. Nevirapine decreases abiraterone levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable, the abiraterone dosage frequency should be increased from once daily to twice daily. 7. Nevirapine reduces acalabrutinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If a strong CYP3A4 inducer is required, the acalabrutinib dose should be increased to 200 mg twice daily. 8. Acetazolamide increases nevirapine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear but minor. 9. Nevirapine decreases alfentanil levels or effects through CYP3A4 induction. The clinical relevance is uncertain but minor. 10. Nevirapine reduces alfuzosin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 11. Nevirapine decreases almotriptan levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 12. Nevirapine reduces alosetron levels or effects through CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unclear but minor. 13. Nevirapine decreases alprazolam levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 14. Nevirapine reduces ambrisentan levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is uncertain but minor. 15. Nevirapine decreases amiodarone levels or effects through CYP3A4 induction. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Nevirapine reduces amitriptyline levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear but minor. 17. Nevirapine decreases amlodipine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 18. Amobarbital reduces nevirapine levels or effects through CYP3A4 induction. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 19. Anastrozole increases nevirapine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear but minor. 20. Apalutamide significantly reduces nevirapine levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Strong CYP3A4 inducers lower systemic exposure to CYP3A4 substrates, potentially reducing therapeutic efficacy. 21. Nevirapine decreases apremilast levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided, as it significantly reduces systemic exposure to apremilast, potentially leading to loss of efficacy. 22. Nevirapine reduces aprepitant levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 23. Nevirapine decreases aripiprazole levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 24. Nevirapine reduces armodafinil levels or effects through CYP3A4 induction. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 25. Nevirapine significantly reduces artemether/lumefantrine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced antimalarial efficacy. 26. Nevirapine decreases artesunate levels or effects by increasing metabolism. Co-administration may reduce the active metabolite (DHA) levels, necessitating monitoring for decreased efficacy. 27. Both atazanavir and nevirapine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Co-administration requires close monitoring. 28. Atazanavir increases nevirapine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while nevirapine reduces atazanavir levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance of these interactions is unclear but minor. 29. Nevirapine may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) should be discontinued at least one month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 30. Nevirapine reduces atogepant levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 31. Nevirapine decreases atorvastatin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Nevirapine reduces avanafil levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients with erectile dysfunction should be closely monitored for reduced efficacy. 33. Nevirapine increases avapritinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 34. Nevirapine significantly reduces axitinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 35. Nevirapine decreases bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 36. Nevirapine significantly reduces bedaquiline levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided due to the risk of reduced therapeutic efficacy. 37. Nevirapine decreases benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required, especially when discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers, as plasma hydrocodone levels may increase, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 38. Nevirapine may interfere with the manufacturing of betibeglogene autotemcel. ART should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 39. Nevirapine reduces bexarotene levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 40. Nevirapine and black cohosh may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of hepatotoxicity. Close monitoring is recommended. 41. Nevirapine decreases bortezomib levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Bosentan reduces nevirapine levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction, while nevirapine decreases bosentan levels or effects through the same mechanism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unclear but minor. 43. Nevirapine significantly reduces bosutinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 44. Nevirapine decreases brexpiprazole levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required, with a potential need to double the brexpiprazole dose over 1–2 weeks. 45. Nevirapine significantly reduces brigatinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 46. Nevirapine decreases budesonide levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 47. Nevirapine reduces bupivacaine levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 48. Nevirapine decreases buprenorphine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required, especially for subdermal implants or long-acting injections. 49. Nevirapine reduces buspirone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 50. Nevirapine decreases cabazitaxel levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or therapy should be modified. 51. Nevirapine increases cabozantinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 52. Nevirapine significantly reduces cabozantinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 53. Nevirapine reduces calcifediol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 54. Nevirapine decreases cannabidiol levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended, with a potential need to increase cannabidiol dosage. 55. Carbamazepine significantly reduces nevirapine levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance to NNRTIs. 56. Nevirapine decreases cariprazine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the unclear net effect on cariprazine exposure. 57. Nevirapine reduces caspofungin levels or effects by increasing metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear but minor. 58. Cenobamate reduces nevirapine levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required, with a potential need to increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates. 59. Ceritinib increases nevirapine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while nevirapine reduces ceritinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 60. Nevirapine decreases cevimeline levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear but minor. 61. Nevirapine reduces cilostazol levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
